newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Philippine foreign secretary Domingo Siazon said on Monday the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) decision to admit Cambodia as a member could still change depending on the internal situation in that country. (PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- The government said the estimated 500 Filipinos in Cambodia were safe and it did not see a need to evacuate them "at this time" (PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Environment Secretary Victor Ramos defends his statements on pollution at Boracay beach saying he did not make a volte face. Ramos has been criticised for revealing that Boracay's waters were infected with disease-causing bacteria and later saying that the pollution was not all that bad. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas defended the peso against a fresh attack on Monday, raising its key money market rate to two-year highs after foreign exchange intervention failed to keep speculators at bay (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
